title: A finite surjection splits finitely many separated etale maps into opens
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $(u_i:U_i\to S)_{i\in I}$ be a finite family of separated etale morphisms of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. There exists a finite surjective morphism $r:T\to S$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism] such that for every $i\in I$ there are a finite set $J_i$, quasi-compact open subschemes $W_{ij}\subseteq T$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and a $T$-isomorphism
$$U_i\times_ST\simeq\coprod_{j\in J_i}W_{ij}.$$
The maps from the summands to $T$ are their open immersions. The opens $W_{ij}$ need not be disjoint as subsets of $T$ and need not cover $T$. Empty $U_i$ and the empty family are allowed. Fibre products are [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Orgogozo author draft, Lemma 9.1.3 and its proof, printed p. 20; the finite-family version follows by successive finite surjective base changes. Local archival PDF WANTED; source read online.
